message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | Key Points | |------|--------------|------------| | **1. Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | • If the first card is an action card, its effect applies to the first player. | | **2. Turn Order** | • Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a “Reverse” card is played). | • The goal is to be the first to play all your cards. | | **3. Playing a Card** | • On your turn, you may play one card that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile.
• If the drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | • You can only play one card per turn unless you’re using special rules (e.g., “Draw Two” combos). | | **4. Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Draw Two (+2)** – Next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – Player chooses the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – Player chooses the next color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn. | • Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no matching color card (otherwise you can be challenged). | | **5. “Uno” Call** | • When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn.
• If you forget and another player calls you out, you must draw two penalty cards. | • Failure to call “UNO” when you have two cards left also results in a penalty. | | **6. Winning a Round** | • The round ends when a player discards their last card.
• Score points:
 – Number cards: face value.
 – Skip/Reverse/Draw Two: 20 points each.
 – Wild/Wild Draw Four: 50 points each.
• Add the points of the other players’ remaining cards to the winner’s score. | • First player to reach 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total) wins the game. | | **7. Optional Variations** | • **Stacking** – Some groups allow stacking Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards.
• **Custom Rules** – e.g., “Draw Two” can be replaced with “Draw Three.” | • Clarify rules before starting to avoid confusion. | **Quick Tips** - Keep track of the current color and number on the discard pile. - Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. - Pay attention to the “UNO” rule—missing it costs you extra cards. Enjoy playing Uno!
